projects.title: Document OCR pipeline
projects.headline: Paperwork in, clean data out.
projects.oneLiner: A template-driven document OCR platform I built solo at Talentnet. Admins define what to extract; a vision-language model reads each page, rules check the fields, and operators review and export Excel. Two months after go-live, 8,000 pages processed, with accuracy 99.6% and about 300 hours saved.

approach.title: Read the page

approach.title: Find every field

approach.title: Check it against the rules
approach.body: Rules catch what a model alone would let through, like a total that doesn't add up.

approach.title: Hand over clean data

projects.note: Illustrated with a made-up invoice. Talentnet's documents and code stay private.
projects.body:
I built this pipeline solo at Talentnet, where I've worked as an AI Engineer Specialist since September 2025. It runs in production.

## How it works

A vision-language model reads each document as an image, so the layout is part of what it sees. A schema tells it which fields to look for, and every field it finds gets a box and a name.

A model alone will let some mistakes through, like a total that doesn't add up. A rule layer checks the extracted fields before anything moves on, and what comes out is structured data, ready for the next system.

## Results

Two months after go-live:

- 7 templates in use.
- 8,000 pages processed.
- Average processing time about 800 ms per page.
- Accuracy 99.6%.
- About 300 hours saved.

Talentnet's documents and code stay private. The illustration on the home page uses a made-up invoice, not a real document.

projects.body:
I built this payroll assistant on my own at Talentnet. It runs in production and answers questions from Vietnamese legal documents.

## Why citations break

Vietnamese legal texts nest. A _Điều_ (article) holds _Khoản_ (clauses), and a _Khoản_ holds _Điểm_ (points). If you cut the text into fixed-size pieces, a passage forgets where it came from, and an answer built on it can't say which rule it is quoting.

## The Tag Chunker

My Tag Chunker keeps the full path, _Điều › Khoản › Điểm_, on every chunk, so nothing is cited from nowhere. Each answer points to the correct document and to a reference a payroll team can cite.

## What I can't show

Talentnet's documents and code stay private. The illustration on the home page uses placeholder text, not real legal content.

projects.title: DVP · payroll data validation
projects.headline: Every client, its own rules — turned into code.
projects.oneLiner: In HR outsourcing payroll, each client has distinct rules and data formats. AI converts client rules into code and reads varied formats dynamically, automating payroll generation and replacing the manual checker step to greatly reduce manual work.

approach.body: Each HR outsourcing client runs payroll by its own rules, in its own data formats.

approach.title: Turn the rules into code
approach.body: AI converts each client's rules into code, so what a person once checked by hand now runs by itself.

approach.title: Read the file, whatever it looks like

approach.title: Generate and check in one pass
approach.body: Payroll is generated and validated automatically — the manual checker step is replaced and manual work drops.

projects.body:
In HR outsourcing payroll, no two clients are alike: each one has distinct rules and a different data format. Keeping up means either hand-tailoring every client or leaving a person to check every run.

This project takes the other path. AI converts each client's rules into code, so the rules stop being tribal knowledge and start being executable. The pipeline reads the client's data formats dynamically instead of one fixed template, so a new client's files don't mean a rebuild.

Payroll generation is automated, and validation runs inside that pass — the separate manual checker step is replaced, which greatly reduces the manual work in payroll.

## What I can't show

Client rules, file formats and payroll data stay private. The illustration on the home page uses made-up values.

projects.title: Poet
projects.headline: A site for a youth charity.
projects.oneLiner: A website for POET, a youth charity in Vietnam. It tells the story of school visits and the time spent with the children, and it takes donations through PayOS.
projects.body:
POET is a youth charity. The site carries their line: tuổi trẻ, nhiệt huyết, nghệ thuật. Young people show up at schoolhouses, spend time with the children, and keep the stories.

The public site is static pages on GitHub Pages: home, the team, corporate Đồng hành packages, and an individual Ủng hộ page. Donations are created in the browser and confirmed by a PayOS webhook on a Cloudflare Worker. A gift appears on the public wall only after an admin publishes it.
